subject: Renewal packaging & mid-contract expansion: consolidation options
messages:
From: Maya Singh <m.singh@acmelabs.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Packaging options for mid-year expansion and co-term alignment

Hi Diego,

Quick note — we're seeing a sustained uplift in inference usage across two teams and expect to need ~40% more capacity from Jan through Jun 2027. Procurement asked me to check what packaging options exist for: (a) adding capacity mid-contract, (b) getting that capacity aligned to our annual renewal date (co-term), and (c) any discounts or onboarding credits available for that uplift.

Current contract: annual commit (12/01/2025 - 11/30/2026), committed units: 1.2M token-units / month. We want to expand immediately and avoid a messy double-billing cadence.

Can you share 1–2 concrete proposals (pricing, timing, billing mechanics) we can run by finance? Also open to a quick call this week.

Thanks,
Maya Singh
Procurement Lead — Acme Labs

--
Acme Labs | procurement@acme.com
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <m.singh@acmelabs.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 11:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Packaging options for mid-year expansion and co-term alignment

Hi Maya — thanks for the context and congrats on the strong adoption. I put together two pragmatic paths below; attaching a short spreadsheet with usage and a draft proposal (acme-proposal-v2.pdf).

Option A — On-demand uplift + pro-rate to annual (low friction)
- Immediate +40% capacity at current unit rates.
- One-off pro-rated invoice for the remainder of the current month.
- On renewal (next annual), we co-term and fold the uplift into the annual committed volume at a modest 8% volume discount.
- Minimal paperwork; fastest time to market.

Option B — Blended mid-contract amendment (preferred for predictability)
- Create an amendment that increases committed units by 40% for the remainder of the contract period.
- Apply a blended discount on the new uplifted volume: 12% for the incremental units (tiered), resulting in an effective blended rate ~9% lower than current.
- Co-term on renewal with true-up at next billing cycle.
- Includes one-time onboarding credit to offset migration costs (we can offer $12k credit).

If helpful, I can pull finance into a 30-min call to walk through numbers. Do you have availability Thu 12/3 10am PT?

Attachments: acme-proposal-v2.pdf, usage-metrics-nov2026.csv

Best,
Diego Fernandez

Looping you both in — Acme (Maya) asked for concrete pricing/mechanics for a mid-contract +40% uplift and co-term at next renewal. Current contract ends 2026-11-30 (they referenced dates in their note). Key constraints: they want minimal billing churn and prefer the uplift folded into the annual commit at renewal. They also asked about onboarding credits.

Quick asks for pricing ops:
- What discount range can we offer for a blended amendment that adds 40% incremental committed units for the remaining contract period and folds into the next annual?
- Can we put a $12k onboarding credit in an amendment without finance sign-off?
- Any SLA carveouts needed for the uplift (they might request slightly higher priority for burst windows)?

I've pasted my proposed Option A/B below from the customer email to give you context.

"Option A — Immediate uplift at current unit rates; co-term at renewal with ~8% volume discount on renewal."
"Option B — Amendment with 12% incremental discount on uplift; $12k onboarding credit; co-term on renewal."

Advice fast appreciated — I have a call Friday with their finance lead and want to present a firm recommendation.

Thanks,
Diego
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Packaging options for mid-year expansion and co-term alignment

Diego — good thread. Quick guidance:

- Discounting: For a mid-contract amendment of this size (40% uplift), finance will typically approve a 10–14% discount on the incremental volume if we secure a commitment to carry through renewal (co-term). That matches Option B.
- Onboarding credit: $12k is reasonable as a one-time offset; treat it as an onboarding credit (applied as a credit memo) and include a clause that it is forfeited if they terminate within 90 days. No separate finance pre-approval needed for up to $15k — I can sign off.
- SLA: Offer a burst-priority window (non-SLA, operational best-effort) during ramp. If they ask for SLA guarantee, escalate to Legal/Finance; avoid hard SLA exceptions.

Suggested commercial language to present to Acme:
1) Amendment adding +40% committed units, incremental volume priced at a 12% discount (applies only to the uplifted units through contract end).
2) At renewal, uplift folds into annual commit; blended renewal rate equals weighted average of existing and uplifted volumes with an overall 9% effective discount applied to the total annual volume.
3) One-time onboarding credit: $12,000 (credit memo).
4) Billing: pro-rated invoice for the amendment period; renewal invoice aligns to 12/01/2027 - 11/30/2028.

Ben — if that discount band is okay, I can cut the amendment and legal can scope a short addendum. Diego, propose we give Acme Option B as the recommended path and offer a 30-min walk-through Friday if they want.

-Lauren

Maya — thanks again for the details and the candid timeline. After internal alignment, here is the recommended path we can execute quickly: 

Summary of recommended path (Option B — amendment + co-term)
- Amendment: increase committed units by 40% effective immediately. Incremental units for the remainder of the contract period will be priced at a 12% discount off list.
- Onboarding: one-time $12,000 onboarding credit applied as a credit memo (forfeited if contract terminates within 90 days).
- Billing: pro-rated invoice for the amendment period (we'll bill the uplift for the remainder of the current cycle).
- Renewal: uplift folds into your next annual period; effective blended renewal discount across total volume will be ~9% (this is the combined effect of current pricing + incremental discount).

Next steps:
1) I attached the draft amendment and a short usage extract for Nov (usage-metrics-nov2026.csv) and a clean PDF proposal (acme-proposal-v2.pdf).
2) Please confirm if you want us to proceed with Option B and we'll route to Legal for the amendment and to DocuSign for signature.
3) If you'd like a short walk-through, Fri 12/10 10am PT works from our side — otherwise we can proceed asynchronously.
